domain: E-commerce order management (online shop backend split into catalog, customer, inventory, payment and order services behind a gateway)
summary:
This is the backend of an online shop. The shown code lets shoppers list products, register a customer account, look up a customer, place orders and list their orders. It lets staff add priced products, check stock for a product and look up the payments recorded for an order. Placing an order is the central flow.

When an order is placed, the order service checks that the customer is active. It reserves stock for each item, looks up each item's price from the catalog, then charges payment as the last step. The order is only committed once the charge succeeds, and a failure returns the failing step's own message. If a step fails, stock already reserved is released through an idempotent inventory compensation route. A payment-void route also exists in the payment service, but the shown order code does not call it. A declined charge writes no payment record.

The services are separate HTTP services. A gateway routes requests by path prefix and strips internal-caller headers from outside requests. It verifies bearer tokens only when an issuer is configured. An order-placed event is published and the inventory service consumes it without handling a message twice, but that handler only logs the payload. A scheduled restock job also runs. Evidence scope: the shown source excerpts. Deployment, monitoring and legacy-format conversion material is excluded, and nothing here is runtime-verified.

useCases.title: Place an order
useCases.description: A customer submits an order with one or more items and quantities. The shop rejects an invalid request or an inactive customer, reserves stock, prices the lines and charges payment last, and returns the placed order.
steps: Customer submits their id and items with positive quantities
An invalid request is rejected with an error message
The order service asks the customer service whether the account is active and refuses if it is not
Stock is reserved for each item and its unit price is fetched from the catalog
A pending order is saved and the total is charged through the payment service
The order is marked placed and an 'order placed' event is published in the same transaction
Any failure is returned to the customer as a conflict with the failing step's message
useCases.evidence: POST /orders handler placeOrder; Service.PlaceOrder; saga.CreateOrder (inventory → payments); PlaceOrderRequest binding rules

useCases.title: Have a failed order release its reserved stock
useCases.description: When a step of order placement fails, completed steps are compensated in reverse order. Reserved stock is released through an idempotent inventory route and the customer sees the step's own error such as 'out of stock'. The payment service also has a route that voids captured payments, but the shown order code does not call it.
steps: A step fails, for example stock is short or the charge is declined
The saga compensates completed steps in reverse order
Reserved quantities are released through inventory's compensation route, keyed by saga id and product
The order transaction rolls back so no order is left behind
The customer receives the failing step's message

useCases.title: View my past orders
useCases.description: A customer lists the orders placed under their user id, with their order lines.
steps: Customer requests their orders
The user id is taken from the request context
Orders for that customer are returned with their lines

useCases.title: Browse the product catalog
useCases.description: A shopper lists all products, each with SKU, name, price and category id.
steps: Shopper requests the product list
The catalog returns every product
useCases.evidence: GET /products handler listProducts; Service.List; Product model

useCases.title: Add a product to the catalog
useCases.description: Shop staff add a product with SKU, name and a price. Products with a missing SKU or name, or a non-positive price, are rejected.
steps: Admin submits the product's SKU, name and price
The request is rejected if required fields are missing or the price is not positive
The product is saved with an assigned id
The stored product is returned

useCases.title: Register a customer account
useCases.description: A new shopper registers with an email and name. The account is created active by default.
steps: Shopper submits an email and name
A missing name or invalid email is rejected
The customer is saved and returned
A storage failure such as a duplicate email is reported as a conflict
useCases.evidence: POST /customers handler registerCustomer; Service.Register; Customer binding rules

useCases.title: Look up a customer's account details
useCases.description: A caller retrieves a customer record by id, including email, name and active flag.
steps: Caller requests a customer by id
A non-numeric id is rejected
The customer is loaded, or not found is returned
The customer record is returned

useCases.title: Block ordering for inactive customers
useCases.description: Before an order proceeds, the order service asks the customer service whether the account is active, and an inactive customer is refused. The call is retried with backoff on transport or server errors.
steps: The order service calls the customer service's is-active route
The customer service looks up the account and returns its active flag
An inactive account stops the order with 'customer inactive'
useCases.evidence: POST /v1/customers/is_active; Service.IsActive; orders clients/customers IsActive; PlaceOrder

useCases.title: Price order items from the catalog
useCases.description: Each ordered product's unit price comes from the catalog and the line totals are summed into the order total. The catalog may serve a price from a per-instance cache for up to 30 seconds.
steps: The order service asks the catalog for each product's price
The catalog returns the price, or not found for an unknown product
The price is stored on the order line and added to the total
useCases.evidence: POST /v1/catalog/price_of; Service.PriceOf with priceCacheTTL; orders clients/catalog PriceOf

useCases.title: Reserve stock for ordered items
useCases.description: Stock is reserved for a product only if on-hand minus reserved covers the quantity, and the stock row is locked during reservation. The inventory service also consumes order-placed events without reprocessing a redelivered message, but its handler only logs the payload.
steps: The order service asks inventory to reserve a product quantity
Inventory locks the stock row and checks available units
The reserved count is increased, or a not-reserved answer is returned
An unknown product returns not found
Order-placed events are de-duplicated by message id before being logged
useCases.evidence: POST /v1/inventory/reserve; reserveHandler; Service.Reserve; OnOrderPlaced; SubscribeOrderPlaced with Idempotent

useCases.title: Check the stock level of a product
useCases.description: A caller reads the on-hand and reserved counts for one product by product id. Errors are returned as problem+json.
steps: Caller requests a stock item by product id
A non-positive or non-numeric id is rejected
The stock item is loaded, or not found is returned
On-hand and reserved counts are returned

useCases.title: Have under-stocked products replenished automatically
useCases.description: A scheduled job sets on-hand to reserved plus 10 for stock items whose on-hand is below reserved. It runs every minute.
steps: A timer fires every minute
The restock update is run
Failures are logged
useCases.evidence: Service.Restock; StartRestockJob; jobs.Run with advisory-lock lease

useCases.title: Pay for an order
useCases.description: A charge is validated, the external payment provider is asked to capture it, and a captured payment record is saved in the same transaction. A provider decline is reported as an error and no record is saved.
steps: The order service posts the order id and amount to payments
The request is rejected if the order id is missing or the amount is negative or not a number
The payment gateway is asked to capture the amount
On success a captured payment is saved
On decline an error is returned and nothing is saved

useCases.title: Look up the payments recorded for an order
useCases.description: A caller retrieves the payment records for an order id, each with amount and status, or not found when there are none.
steps: Caller requests payments for an order id
An invalid id is rejected
The payment records are loaded in id order
The records are returned, or not found if none exist

useCases.title: Use the shop through a single authenticated entry point
useCases.description: The gateway routes requests by longest path prefix to the catalog, customer, inventory, payment and order services. When an issuer is configured, it requires a valid bearer token. It strips internal-caller headers so outsiders cannot pose as services.
steps: A caller sends a request to the gateway
When an issuer is configured, a missing or invalid bearer token gets 401
The internal-caller and token headers are removed from the request
The request goes to the service with the longest matching prefix, otherwise to the legacy upstream or 404
